name_note: The GTDB genus Fannyhessea covers genomes that NCBI still labels Atopobium; the vaginal species appears in older papers as Atopobium vaginae.

sentences.text: Fannyhessea vaginae, previously named Atopobium vaginae, is an anaerobic Gram-positive organism commonly associated with the female genital flora.
Rare invasive infections have been reported, including bacteraemia with vertebral osteomyelitis in an older male who had signs of urinary tract infection.
In a clinical study it was highly sensitive for bacterial vaginosis and more specific for the condition than Gardnerella vaginalis.
In culture it triggers an innate immune response, raising interleukin-6, interleukin-8 and beta-defensin 4 transcripts in vaginal epithelial cells.
